item.title: Steady on: Meta's AI billions and the silent Fed
item.description:
The Fed left interest rates unchanged (for now)...
Get ready for a thrill. A Six Flags theme park in New Jersey unveiled plans to build a new roller coaster it says will break six world records. The park says that when the coaster, named Bakunawa after a serpent from Philippine legend, opens next year, it will be the world’s: 1) fastest spinning coaster (zooming 100 miles per hour) 2) fastest inversion 3) first upside down launch 4) longest stall inversion 5) tallest spinning coaster and 6) first floorless spinning coaster. We don’t know if there’s a world record for getting sickest on an amusement park ride, but we bet we could break that one, too, if we get the chance to visit.
https://www.morningbrew.com/issues/steady-on

item.description:
Why the tech industry cares about open-weight AI...
Hello there. Police are looking for two men who sneaked up to the top of the Seattle Space Needle with parachutes on, flipped over a glass wall, and floated down the 605 feet to the ground before disappearing. This happened around 8:50pm local time on Friday night. The most bizarre part for us is how anyone has that kind of energy to spare at the end of the workweek.

item.title: Business Travel Brew: Private jets versus shared hotel rooms
item.description:
Keeping the receipts on corporate excursions...
Good morning. Put on that spiffy blazer and charge your devices, because the Brew’s taking you on a business trip. Today’s special edition will highlight the latest business travel trends, from “bleisure” becoming the standard to Orlando’s rise as the US’ top corporate meeting spot. We’ll also recommend some of pop culture’s best business travel moments and debate whether your boss should be able to ask you to share a hotel room with Bill from IT. Welcome to Business Travel Brew!
